FINAL BUZZER

## FINAL BUZZER

is our closing huddle where coaches see the players off as a group. The Final Buzzer should take no more than 5 minutes to maximize player attention spans. There are five parts that should be covered in every Final Buzzer:

CALL IN

Players are verbally called in to huddle up and stand in a circle with all players and coaches if numbers allow (for larger groups, coaches may need to stand in front of the players).

CONNECTIONS

Players are given connections by the coaches as they join the Tip-Off (example of connections: high five, fist bump, handshake, pat on the shoulder).

COMMUNICATIONS

Players are delivered any relevant news or information for the day. This can include rules, expectations, directions to the bathroom, expectations for water break, etc.

CONCLUSION

Players are debriefed on the learnings and prepared for the end of the module.

CHEER

Players and coaches give an enthusiastic and excited cheer together!

CONNECTIONS

Players are given connections by the coaches as they join the Tip-Off (example of connections: high five, fist bump, handshake, pat on the shoulder).

COMMUNICATIONS

Players are delivered any relevant news or information for the day. This can include rules, expectations, directions to the bathroom, expectations for water break, etc.

COMMENCEMENT

Players are primed and prepped for the start of the camp.

CHEER

WARM-UP

Basketball School

PASS TOUCHDOWN

10 MIN

BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available half-court spaces

### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per half-court

### DESCRIPTION

Players will divide into two teams in each half-court. This can be played with numbers from anywhere from 3-on-3 to 8-on-8. The aim of the game is to score a touchdown in the opposing teams endzone, which is any area past the sideline. Players are not allowed to dribble. A change of possession occurs on any steal or violation (e.g. travel, out of bounds, etc).

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Players can take one dribble every catch.
- Players can only pass with their weak hand
- Players can dribble sideways or backwards, but not forwards.
- Change the type of ball instead of using a basketball (e.g. a tennis ball, volleyball, etc).

### SCORING

1 point for touchdown, first team to 5 points wins.

### STAFF ROLE

- Ensure players keep track of their scores. No communicated score = no point!
- Encourage players to exploit space

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Passing and ball movement
- Moving without the ball
- Creating space and keeping advantage

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- How can you connect with your teammates?
- What could you do defensively to disrupt your opponents?

OBSTACLE COURSE TAG

10 MIN

BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available half-court spaces

### EQUIPMENT

Cones. Can add 1 ball per player for dribbling loads.

### DESCRIPTION

Divide the players into different half-court spaces, with a minimum of eight players and a maximum of 20 players. Give anywhere from two to four players within each half-court a cone. They start as the taggers, but as soon as they have tagged someone, they must give them the cone and begin to escape. Players must stay in the half-court space and cannot step out of bounds.

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Add some obstacles into the course. These could include plastic chairs or coaches! The players must play their tag games while using the obstacles to evade the taggers.
- Add a ball for dribbling.
- Players can only use their weak hand to dribble.

### SCORING

N/A

### STAFF ROLE

- Move (safe) obstacles into the playing area.
- Ensure players do not step out of bounds.

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Exploiting space

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- How can you interact or use the obstacles to avoid the taggers?

GAME TIME

Basketball School

GAME TIME

is where players participate in different activities and games designed to stimulate their growth and development.

These activities have been carefully created to mimic the game of basketball. With the NBA Basketball School Camp Curriculum, players develop technically and tactically through the actual act of playing basketball itself.

Each Game Time activity is clearly described and presented in the following format: name, time, space, equipment, description, scoring, types of loads, staff roles, key concepts, and guiding questions. Coaches are encouraged to utilize the information presented and to expand on those ideas in a way that would be most meaningful to their players.

GAME TIME

Basketball School

### I-ON-I BIG ADVANTAGE SHOOTING

16 MIN

BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available half-court spaces

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per group

#### DESCRIPTION

The offensive player will stand in a shooting position outside of the paint, at a range that they are comfortable shooting from. The defender will begin at least four big steps away from the offensive player. The defender could be in front of, side on, diagonal to or even behind the offensive player. As soon as they pass the ball, they will closeout and attempt to contest the shot. The shooter must shoot the ball before the defender can alter the shot. After three shots have been taken from different locations, the players switch roles.

#### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points or 3 points for made baskets.

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Adaptive shooting
- Closing out to shooting hand

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- The shooter must take one dribble and shoot off the dribble each-time.
- The defender can vary their pass (e.g. high pass, bounce pass, spin pass, rolling the ball on the floor, etc).
- The offensive player can drive or shoot immediately.

#### STAFF ROLE

- Remind the players to leave space for the shooters to land on the floor safely.
- Ensure players change location frequently.

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- How could you prepare to shoot quickly?
- Defensively, what is the fastest way to closeout to the shooter?
